neighbours.label: The verb ' sum'/' sums' where 'up' is about to follow ('to sum up', 'sums up'); the card shows the same on other verbs before 'up' (set, lit, open, pick), which probed much weaker
fire: Before we break for lunch, let me briefly sum up what the committee has agreed so far.
That one photograph sums up everything the town went through during the flood.
At the end of the lecture the professor tried to sum up a century of research in two minutes.
Her closing remark neatly sums up the mood of the whole conference.
If I had to sum up the film in a word, I would call it restless.
The final chapter attempts to sum up the lessons of the expedition.
The coach said the last ten minutes sum up the season for his team.
So, to sum up: the bridge is safe, but the road leading to it is not.
quiet: Before we break for lunch, let me briefly summarize what the committee has agreed so far.
That one photograph captures everything the town went through during the flood.
At the end of the lecture the professor worked out the sum of the series on the board.
Her closing remark neatly wraps up the mood of the whole conference.
A large sum of money was found in a suitcase under the bed.
The final chapter attempts to add up the costs of the expedition.
The coach said the last ten minutes showed up every weakness in his team.
So, in short: the bridge is safe, but the road leading to it is not.

notes: Card: ' set' x8, ' lit' x3, ' open' x2, ' sum' x2, peaking on the verb before 'up'; the output direction suppresses ' up' and its variants, and the - pole fires on nouns before 'up' (build up, hold up, line up). Probes: 'sum up' 0.64-0.70, 'lit up/lit a candle' 0.23-0.35, 'set up' 0.14-0.18, 'open up' 0.02, 'the sum of' 0.01. Label covers only the 'sum' part that reached the bar; the wider verb-before-up reading did not fire on short sentences.
